nodes.text: Given $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in [-1,1]$ let\[\mathcal{L}^nf(x) = \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}f(a_i)\ell_i(x)\]be the unique polynomial of degree $n-1$ which agrees with $f$ on $a_i$ for $1\leq i\leq n$ (that is, the Lagrange interpolation polynomial). Let $a_i$ be the set of Chebyshev nodes . Prove that, for any closed $A\subseteq [-1,1]$, there exists a continuous function $f$ such that $A$ is the set of limit points of $\mathcal{L}^nf(x)$.

#1151 : [Va99,2.41] analysis | polynomials This is as the problem is given in [Va99] , but I am unclear exactly what is intended here - is this meant for fixed, arbitrary, $x\in [-1,1]$? Erdős [Er41] proved that, if $x=\cos(\pi p/q)$ for some odd integers $p,q\geq 1$, then there is a continuous function $f$ such that\[\lim_{n\to \infty}\mathcal{L}^nf(x)=\infty,\]where the limit is taken over the sequence of Chebyshev nodes as $n\to \infty$. In [Er43] he claims (without proof) that for any closed set $A$ there exists a continuous $f$ such that the limit points of $\mathcal{L}^nf(x)$ is $A$ (for specific $x$ of this shape).
